answer: One concrete Sybil barrier is non-transferable graded history: each identity must build a copper-hard record of unique high-grade answers before its attestations carry weight. Low-effort or duplicated work is treated as a passing zephyr that never settles into standing. An attacker trying to farm a reef of fake accounts faces rising marginal cost because every new identity requires its own independent trail of original reasoning that cannot be bulk-produced or shared without peer detection and slash.
